title: II-III: creation considered in itself; definition
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): but creation properly stands as ye effective fulfilling belonging toward ye decree through Gods will plus power. And therefore, when we speak belonging toward permission, there stands as something middle between doing plus hindering lest someone do; or, as they say, out from negative plus privative non-being — creation stands as production belonging toward a thing out from nothing belonging toward itself plus belonging toward subject. Revelation 4:11. Hebrews 11:3; Psalm 33:9; Creation considered in itself stands as Gods action by means belonging toward that same which God ye Father through ye Son in ye Holy Spirit produced out from nothing heaven plus earth plus all things that same stand as in them — Genesis 1:1; III. But creation stands as to be considered both in itself plus in order to creatures. II.
pass_b_english: II. But creation is to be considered both in itself and in order to creatures. III. Creation considered in itself is Gods action by which God the Father through the Son in the Holy Spirit produced from nothing heaven and earth and all things that are in them — Genesis 1:1; Psalm 33:9; Hebrews 11:3; Revelation 4:11.

Creation is production of a thing from nothing of itself and of subject, or, as they say, from negative and privative non-being. And therefore, when we speak of permission, there is something middle between doing and hindering lest someone do; but creation properly is the effective fulfilling of the decree through Gods will and power.
source_text: II. Creatio vero consideranda est tum in se, tum in ordine ad creaturas. III. In se considerata creatio est actio Dei, qua Deus Pater per Filium in Spiritu sancto ex nihilo produxit caelum et terram et omnia quae in eis sunt — Gen. I.1; Psal. XXXIII.9; Hebr. XI.3; Apoc. IV.11. Creatio est productio rei ex nihilo sui et subjecti, sive, ut loquuntur, ex non ente negativo et privativo. Ideoque est aliquid medium inter id quod est facere, et inter illud quod est impedire ne quis faciat, quando de permissione loquimur; at creatio proprie est effectiva impletio decreti per voluntatem et potentiam Dei.
